query: A second independent international cable route will preserve connectivity after failure.
Geographically diverse domestic fibre routes will eliminate single points of communications failure.
Satellite or microwave backup links will maintain connectivity when fibre fails.
A second international telecommunications operator will provide an alternative connection if the primary provider fails.
Critical facilities will receive two independent communications links for service continuity.
Redundant network nodes and exchanges will maintain communications after node failure.
Redundant network architecture will maintain connectivity after communications failure.
